source.title: Trade-offs of Local SGD at Scale: An Empirical Study
source.authors: J. J. Ortiz; Jonathan Frankle; Michael G. Rabbat; Ari S. Morcos; Nicolas Ballas

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports ImageNet results that qualify earlier claims about local SGD and generalization: accuracy depends on worker count, local steps, switching point, learning-rate schedule, and task scale. It does not test most of the catalog versions directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports ImageNet and TinyImageNet accuracy results for local and post-local SGD. These bear on V5's large-batch training setting, though the local-update method and communication pattern also change. Results cited from other studies are not rows. Values read only from plots are recorded as figure only; the paper describes the principal trends in text.
record.test_reason: Increasing workers at fixed per-worker batch size increases global batch size under a fixed 90-epoch budget. These comparisons test V5 in synchronous, local and post-local SGD settings. Comparisons that vary synchronization frequency or switching time alone do not test batch-size effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors additionally unify worker count and local steps through their product, report that SlowMo improves accuracy without additional communication, and conclude that switching to local SGD benefits generalization briefly but harms final accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Studies local and post-local SGD communication patterns on image classification, rather than the ordinary large-batch training comparisons in V5. Uses ResNet architectures, fixed epoch budgets, and ImageNet-1k plus TinyImageNet.
record.method_sensitivity: Worker count; local steps; switching epoch; step-wise versus half-cosine learning-rate schedule; dataset/task scale; SlowMo addition; LARS optimizer.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing local steps reduces training and validation accuracy; later switching and the learning-rate schedule change the communication-versus-accuracy trade-off.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local and post-local SGD on ImageNet trade reduced synchronization for lower accuracy, with performance depending on switching time and learning-rate schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-local SGD after the first learning-rate decay improves accuracy over synchronous SGD on TinyImageNet, unlike the principal ImageNet results.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The accuracy benefit of post-local SGD depends on the task and training setting.

fits_no_version.finding: SlowMo improves local and post-local SGD accuracy without additional communication but does not fully close the synchronous-SGD accuracy gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Slow momentum mitigates accuracy losses from reduced synchronization.

fits_no_version.finding: Switching to local SGD temporarily lowers validation error while increasing training error, but harms final accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local-SGD switching has a transient regularization benefit that does not predict improved final accuracy.

record.problems: The authors state that the work studies only ImageNet-1k as its primary task, with limited supplementary TinyImageNet experiments. Results are reported as medians over ten seeds, but no error bars are stated in the supplied text. Many accuracy values are only plotted, without precise textual values. Large-batch effects are not isolated from local-SGD synchronization effects.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results omitted. Figure 6's aggregate trend by K×H is described in text but is not separately rowed because it restates the worker/local-step effects already captured in R2-R4. Figure 14 also restates the training/validation error pattern in R13.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization comparisons.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Adaptive-versus-SGD optimizer comparisons under limited or broader tuning.

Language models; batches beyond the tested accuracy-comparison range; an unadapted recipe; controlled tests of longer training, scaling/warmup removal, or normalization and regularization changes as remedies. Scaling and warmup are used throughout, so their causal benefit is not isolated.
Dropout and its interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Increasing H does not increase batch size: it increases local updates between synchronizations. Consequently, most extracted rows concern local-SGD optimization rather than V5. The synchronous baseline's lack of a penalty supports an explicit exception already included in V5; it does not challenge that qualified version. Exact accuracy differences cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied figure text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence; random-label held-out performance.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD or momentum SGD under different tuning regimes.

The paper varies worker count and local synchronization frequency, but does not isolate ordinary large-batch training from local-SGD effects or test language models. It does not test longer training, warmup or normalization changes as remedies against a large-batch penalty.
Dropout and its interaction with training-set size, data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, norm- or margin-based measures, and their association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Minibatch SGD baseline as worker count increases
rows.value: The minibatch baseline does not experience the accuracy trade-off as worker count increases.
rows.uncertainty: Median performance over ten independent runs; no error bar stated.
rows.note: The text explicitly contrasts the minibatch baseline with local and post-local SGD; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Specify global batches of 256, 512, 1024 and 2048, with linear learning-rate scaling and five-epoch warmup. The absence of an accuracy penalty is consistent with V5's adapted-recipe exception.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3; Section 5.1, Figures 4–5 and increasing-workers paragraph.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Local SGD as worker count increases
rows.baseline: Minibatch SGD at corresponding worker count
rows.value: Both training and validation results worsen as worker count increases.
rows.uncertainty: Median performance over ten independent runs; no error bar stated.
rows.note: The authors say local SGD does not maintain accuracy as workers increase; curves are shown in the figures.
rows.check: The relevant comparison is across worker counts at fixed H, rather than against minibatch SGD at the corresponding worker count. Per-worker batch is 32; global batch increases from 256 to 2048. Learning-rate scaling and warmup are used.

source_check.correct: The worker-count effect compares local SGD across increasing worker counts at fixed H. The reference is local SGD with fewer workers at the same H; minibatch SGD is a separate comparator. Per-worker batch 32 and workers 8, 16, 32, 64 imply global batches 256, 512, 1024, 2048.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3; Section 5.1, Figures 4–5 and increasing-workers paragraph.
source_check.problem: The baseline names a different-method comparison rather than the reference for the reported worker-count trend.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Post-local SGD as worker count increases
rows.baseline: Minibatch SGD at corresponding worker count
rows.value: Both training and validation results worsen as worker count increases; absolute drops are smaller than for local SGD.
rows.uncertainty: Median performance over ten independent runs; no error bar stated.
rows.note: The authors report a negative accuracy effect, smaller in absolute size than for local SGD, with more communication and runtime.
rows.check: The relevant comparison is across worker counts at fixed H. Smaller absolute drops than local SGD do not establish an incomplete effect: validation accuracy still decreases with increasing global batch under the fixed epoch budget. Scaling and warmup are used.

source_check.correct: The worker-count effect compares post-local SGD across increasing worker counts at fixed H and switching epoch 30. The reference is post-local SGD with fewer workers under those same conditions; minibatch SGD is a separate comparator.
source_check.problem: The baseline names a different-method comparison rather than the reference for the reported worker-count trend.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Increasing local steps between model averages
rows.value: Training and validation accuracy monotonically decrease as local steps increase.
rows.uncertainty: Median performance over ten independent runs; no error bar stated.
rows.note: The stated trend applies to both local and post-local SGD.
rows.check: Increasing local steps changes synchronization frequency, not global batch size. The accuracy decline cannot establish V5's batch-size effect.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Post-local SGD with varied switching point
rows.value: Later switching points improve accuracy at the cost of additional communication.
rows.uncertainty: Median performance over ten independent runs; no error bar stated.
rows.note: The paper reports a similar pattern for ResNet-101, but the plotted values are not specified in text.
rows.check: Switching time varies at fixed worker count and batch size; this measures a communication-versus-accuracy trade-off.

rows.subject: ResNet-101
rows.operation_detail: Post-local SGD with varied switching point
rows.value: Same switching-point pattern as ResNet-50; later switching improves accuracy at the cost of additional communication.
rows.uncertainty: Median performance over ten independent runs; no error bar stated.
rows.note: Exact plotted values are not specified in text.
rows.check: Switching time varies at fixed worker count and batch size; this does not measure a batch-size penalty.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Post-local SGD with varied switching point
rows.value: Validation accuracy has a more monotonic trade-off with switching time; the learning-rate scale at the switch is crucial to keeping the drop minimal.
rows.uncertainty: Median performance over ten independent runs; no error bar stated.
rows.note: The study contrasts this pattern with the step-wise schedule.
rows.check: The cosine-schedule switching comparison holds batch size fixed and does not establish a remedy for a measured batch-size penalty.

rows.subject: ResNet-101
rows.operation_detail: Post-local SGD with varied switching point
rows.value: Validation accuracy has a more monotonic trade-off with switching time; the learning-rate scale at the switch is crucial to keeping the drop minimal.
rows.uncertainty: Median performance over ten independent runs; no error bar stated.
rows.note: The study contrasts this pattern with the step-wise schedule.
rows.check: The cosine-schedule switching comparison holds batch size fixed and does not establish a batch-size effect.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Post-local SGD on TinyImageNet with varied switching point

conditions.value: varied; learning-rate decays at epochs 30 and 50

rows.value: Switching after the first learning-rate decay produces accuracy gains over the synchronous minibatch baseline.
rows.note: The authors contrast this result with ImageNet, where little to no accuracy gains are achieved by switching during training.
rows.check: Gains from switching to local SGD at a given worker count are not a reversal of a batch-size penalty. Add K=16 and K=32 and the 60-epoch budget to the conditions.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Post-local SGD with LARS and varied switching point
rows.baseline: Minibatch SGD with LARS synchronizing every update
rows.value: Early switching reduces accuracy relative to the minibatch baseline; later switching provides some accuracy improvements.
rows.note: The text describes a similar trade-off to SGD and a more linear trend for LARS.
rows.check: This varies switching time with LARS at fixed batch size. It neither tests V5's batch-size effect nor V4's adaptive-versus-SGD comparison.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Adding SlowMo to local and post-local SGD
rows.baseline: Local or post-local SGD without SlowMo
rows.value: SlowMo improves validation accuracy in all tested cases but does not fully bridge the gap to synchronous minibatch SGD.
rows.note: This is a mitigation result; the figure includes ResNet-50 and ResNet-101.
rows.check: SlowMo mitigates the synchronization-related accuracy loss; no small-versus-large-batch comparison establishes mitigation of V5's penalty.

rows.subject: ResNet-101
rows.operation_detail: Adding SlowMo to local and post-local SGD
rows.baseline: Local or post-local SGD without SlowMo
rows.value: SlowMo improves validation accuracy in all tested cases but does not fully bridge the gap to synchronous minibatch SGD.
rows.note: This is a mitigation result; the figure includes ResNet-50 and ResNet-101.
rows.check: SlowMo improves local/post-local SGD at the tested settings, but this comparison does not isolate a batch-size penalty.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Comparing training and validation errors over training for post-local SGD switching points
rows.value: After switching, training error is higher and validation error lower than the minibatch baseline; the long-term effect is detrimental to final accuracy.
rows.note: Authors report that post-local curves follow the same general trajectory after the switch and that the pattern holds across schedules.
rows.check: The transient regularization effect follows a synchronization change at fixed batch size. Higher training error and temporarily lower validation error do not test any listed version.

relationships.condition: ImageNet ResNet-50, local SGD, fixed H=2, 4 or 8, increasing global batch through worker count, 90 epochs
relationships.reason: R2 reports worse validation accuracy as global batch increases, despite learning-rate scaling and warmup; training accuracy also worsens.
relationships.display_finding: Increasing worker count reduced validation and training accuracy relative to fewer workers at the same synchronization period despite scaling and warmup.
